title: Fast charging of quantum batteries assisted by nonlinear couplings
authors: Y. -J. Shen, Y. -C. Shen, C. -H. Chu, H. H. Jen
abstract: Charger-mediated quantum batteries offer promising opportunities for efficient energy transfer and storage at the quantum level, with potential advantages beyond their classical counterparts. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that nonlinear charger-battery interactions can substantially accelerate the charging of quantum batteries. In the weak-driving regime, sufficiently strong nonlinear coupling can dominate over the effect of dephasing and significantly reduce the charging time. In the strong- and optimal-driving regimes, where the optimal driving strength maximizes the steady-state ergotropy in the linear-coupling regime, nonlinear coupling gives rise to a new optimum in the charging time beyond that of the linear-coupling regime, accompanied by nearly critically damped dynamics. Remarkably, even in the absence of external driving, nonlinear coupling alone can substantially reduce the charging time, providing an alternative route toward fast battery charging. Our results establish nonlinear charger-battery coupling as an effective resource for accelerating quantum-battery charging and broaden the scope of interaction-enabled quantum advantages in energy transfer and storage.
summary: This theoretical study demonstrates that incorporating nonlinear couplings between a charger and a quantum battery significantly accelerates the energy charging process. The authors show that this nonlinear interaction acts as a powerful resource, allowing for fast charging even when no external driving field is applied. This broadens the understanding of interaction-enabled quantum advantages in energy storage.
main_problem: The paper investigates how nonlinear couplings can accelerate the charging process of quantum batteries, potentially surpassing the performance limits of classical or linearly coupled quantum systems.
main_result: Nonlinear charger-battery interactions are shown to be an effective resource for accelerating charging, enabling faster charging even in the absence of external driving.
method: The analysis uses theoretical modeling based on the master equation to derive the time evolution of energy and ergotropy in the quantum battery system.
model_or_system: The system consists of a charger coupled to a quantum battery, modeled with a Hamiltonian including linear and nonlinear coupling terms, and subject to external driving and dephasing.
key_observables: Battery Energy (E_B), Ergotropy, and the characteristic Charging Time ($\tau$).
important_parameters: Nonlinear coupling strength ($g_2$), linear coupling strength ($g_1$), external driving strength ($F$), and dephasing rate ($\gamma_C$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the interaction picture under the resonance condition, and the system is modeled using two-level approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of energy and ergotropy under varying coupling strengths and driving conditions, and plot the charging time ($\tau$) dependence on the dephasing rate ($\gamma_C$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the charging dynamics by first establishing the model Hamiltonian, then deriving the equations of motion, and finally comparing the charging time and energy storage capabilities across weak, strong, and undriven regimes, highlighting the role of $g_2$.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems and energy transfer, utilizing concepts like coupling-induced dynamics and non-equilibrium thermodynamics, which are central to AMO physics.
